title: News Failure
teaches: The News Failure as we trade it: big, dated news meets the opposite reaction, a bad-news gap down on heavy volume that is back over the prior close by the close, above the 200-day; the buy is a market order as price trades back over the prior close, the stop sits a few cents under the news day's low (wide, so the size comes from the stop), a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail, and a loss at the stop is the system working. The short is the mirror.

questions.q: In a News Failure long, what does the stock do on the news day?
choices: Gaps down on bad news, then climbs back
Gaps up on good news and holds the gap
Gaps down on bad news and keeps falling
Drifts sideways on no news or gap
questions.answer: Gaps down on bad news, then climbs back
questions.why: Gaps down on bad news, then climbs back over the prior close. The news failed to keep it down.
questions.lesson_line: Bad news, a gap down, and a close back over the prior close.

wrong.Gaps up on good news and holds the gap: That is the News Gapper, good news that holds.
wrong.Gaps down on bad news and keeps falling: News that keeps the stock down worked. It is the bear gap, not a failure.
wrong.Drifts sideways on no news or gap: A News Failure needs a dated catalyst behind a real gap.

questions.q: Shapiro's test: the news is bullish, but by the end of the day the market closes down.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Shapiro: the market fails and closes down in the absence of any other bearish news. That is his news failure.
questions.lesson_line: News points one way and the close goes the other.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A News Failure long is bought as price trades back over the ___ close.
questions.answer: prior
questions.why: Prior. A market order when price trades back over the prior close (red to green) on the news day.
questions.lesson_line: Buy as price trades back over the prior close.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on a News Failure long?
choices: Under the prior day's close
A few cents under the news day's low
A few cents over the news day's high
At 3% under your buy, whatever the chart
questions.answer: A few cents under the news day's low
questions.why: A few cents under the news day's low so far. For a short it goes over the high.
questions.lesson_line: Long: under the news day's low. Short: over its high.

wrong.Under the prior day's close: The news day's low is the extreme. The prior close is the trigger, not the stop.
wrong.A few cents over the news day's high: That is the short's stop, mirrored.
wrong.At 3% under your buy, whatever the chart: The stop is the news day's extreme, not a fixed percent.

questions.q: A News Failure long must be above the 200-day, unless it is a parabolic long.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. No longs below the 200-day, unless it is a parabolic long. The News Failure long follows that rule.
questions.lesson_line: Longs live above the 200-day. The News Failure is no exception.

questions.q: With no news feed, a gap of 4% or more on 2 times the prior 50-day volume stands in for the news.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. With no news feed, the stock opens 4% or more under the prior close. Volume is 2 times or more the prior 50-day average.
questions.lesson_line: No news feed, so a big gap on double volume stands in for it.

questions.q: Good news gaps a stock up, but it closes under the prior close. What is that?
choices: A News Gapper, but a weak one
An Oops Reversal, but with news
A News Failure, the mirror
A bear gap
questions.answer: A News Failure, the mirror
questions.why: A News Failure, the mirror. Good news gaps up and the stock closes red, under the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: Same headline, opposite close: gapper holds, failure fades.

wrong.A News Gapper, but a weak one: A News Gapper closes green and holds the gap.
wrong.An Oops Reversal, but with news: An Oops needs an open under the prior low and has no news requirement.
wrong.A bear gap: A bear gap starts with bad news that keeps the stock down.

questions.q: Bad news gaps a stock down and it closes at the low, staying down. What is it?
choices: A News Failure long on the open
A News Gapper that held its gap
A Red to Green on the second day
A bear gap or earnings breakdown
questions.answer: A bear gap or earnings breakdown
questions.why: A bear gap or an earnings breakdown. If bad news gaps the stock down and it stays down, the news worked.
questions.lesson_line: If the gap down keeps going, the news worked. That is not a failure.

wrong.A News Failure long on the open: The long closes back over the prior close. This stock did not.
wrong.A News Gapper that held its gap: A News Gapper gaps on good news and holds it.
wrong.A Red to Green on the second day: Red to Green reclaims the prior close. This did not.

questions.q: How is the News Failure short entered?
choices: Market, over the prior day's high
Market, back under the prior close
A limit order at the day's high
questions.answer: Market, back under the prior close
questions.why: At market as price trades back under the prior close (green to red). Entries are market orders.
questions.lesson_line: The short mirrors the long: under the prior close.

wrong.Market, over the prior day's high: The trigger is the prior close, not the prior high. The short waits for price to trade back under that close.
wrong.A limit order at the day's high: Entries are market orders when the trigger trades.

questions.q: Five or more stocks with the same News Failure shape on one day usually means the news was the market.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Fewer than 5 such events on the same day is the line. A same-day cluster means the news was the market, not the stock.
questions.lesson_line: A crowd of the same shape on one day means a market story, not a stock story.

questions.q: What price and daily traded value does a News Failure need?
choices: $5 and $5 million a day
$20 and $100 million a day
$10 and $20 million a day
questions.answer: $10 and $20 million a day
questions.why: $10 and $20 million a day. Only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.
questions.lesson_line: Price $10 or more and $20 million or more traded a day.

wrong.$5 and $5 million a day: Too thin. The floor is $10 and $20 million a day.
wrong.$20 and $100 million a day: That is stricter than the rule.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: No new buy or short in the ___ sessions before a scheduled report.
questions.why: 3. No new buy or short in the 3 sessions before a scheduled report.
questions.lesson_line: Three sessions before a report, no new trade.

questions.q: Which close grades the long up?
choices: The bottom 25% of the day's range
Right at the prior close, flat
Top 25%, after undercutting the low
Anywhere green, even by a few cents
questions.answer: Top 25%, after undercutting the low
questions.why: The top 25% of the range, after its low undercut the prior day's low, an Oops shape.
questions.lesson_line: A strong close in the top quarter grades the long up.

wrong.Right at the prior close, flat: A close at the prior close shows no reversal.
wrong.Anywhere green, even by a few cents: A small green close is weak. The strong shape is the top 25%.

questions.q: Shapiro says positioning alone is enough to take the trade.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Trader positioning is not enough to execute the trade; you also need market confirmation.
questions.lesson_line: Crowding is half of it. The failed news is the other half.

questions.q: The stock is already well past the prior close when you look. What is the limit?
choices: Skip if more than 10% past the close
Skip if over 4% past the trigger
Buy any time that day, with a stop
questions.answer: Skip if over 4% past the trigger
questions.why: Skip if the stock already moved more than 4% past the trigger. For a long the trigger is the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: Past 4% beyond the trigger, skip it. Shapiro: I miss a trade, I miss it.

wrong.Skip if more than 10% past the close: The limit is 4% past the trigger.

questions.q: Bought at 86.36 with the stop at 81.48. How far under the buy is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 5.7. That is past our usual 3%, so the size comes from the stop. AAOI's stop was exactly that wide.
questions.lesson_line: Wide stop, small size. Measure the stop in percent first.

questions.q: Bought at 31.83 with the stop at 30.23. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 36.63. One R is the buy minus the stop. Add three of those to the buy. SEDG got there the next day.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before you buy. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: Shapiro's stop is hit only by a close beyond the extreme. What is ours?
choices: The same, a close beyond the extreme
A mental stop, watched all day
A real stop order, hit intraday
questions.answer: A real stop order, hit intraday
questions.why: A real stop order with the broker, hit intraday. Every position has one.
questions.lesson_line: Real stop order, not a mental stop and not a close-only stop.

wrong.The same, a close beyond the extreme: Ours is a real stop order with the broker. It is hit intraday.
wrong.A mental stop, watched all day: A stop kept in your head is not allowed.

questions.q: Once the News Failure trade is on, the stop can be moved wider if it keeps getting close.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The stop only moves in the trade's favor, never wider.
questions.lesson_line: The stop moves only in your favor.

questions.q: How is the last third of a News Failure trailed?
choices: A close beyond the 10-day or 21-day
A close beyond the 200-day average
A fixed 5% under the move's high
questions.answer: A close beyond the 10-day or 21-day
questions.why: A close beyond the 10-day for a fast mover or the 21-day for a steadier one.
questions.lesson_line: The last third rides the trail and leaves on a close beyond it.

wrong.A close beyond the 200-day average: The trail is the 10-day for fast movers or the 21-day for steadier ones.
wrong.A fixed 5% under the move's high: A fixed percent ignores the chart. The trail is the average.

questions.q: A trade gaps through the stop. What decides the new stop?
choices: The prior day's close or the open
The extreme of the first 30 minutes
The 10-day average at the open
questions.answer: The extreme of the first 30 minutes
questions.why: The extreme of the first 30 minutes is the new stop, and if that loss is past 2R, get out.
questions.lesson_line: Gap through the stop: the first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.The prior day's close or the open: The extreme of the first 30 minutes sets the new stop.
wrong.The 10-day average at the open: The 10-day is the trail, not the gap stop.

questions.q: A News Failure still under 1R after 10 sessions is held until the stop or the trail decides.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Under 1R after 10 sessions, out. It frees the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten sessions under 1R, and the money moves on.

questions.q: Does the day pass the gap-and-volume test for news?
choices: No; the gap is under 4%
No; volume must be 5x the average
Yes; the gap and volume both clear
questions.answer: Yes; the gap and volume both clear
questions.why: Yes. The open of 47.80 is more than 4% under the 50.00 close, and the volume is 2.4 times the 50-day average.
questions.lesson_line: A gap of 4% or more on 2 times the volume passes the test.

wrong.No; the gap is under 4%: The open is more than 4% under the prior close, so it clears 4%.
wrong.No; volume must be 5x the average: The test asks for 2 times the 50-day volume or more.

questions.story: A stock closed at 50.00. It opens at 47.80 on 2.4 million shares against a 50-day average of 1.0 million.

questions.q: News Failure or plain Red to Green?
choices: Plain Red to Green; no news gap
News Failure; it reclaimed the close
Neither; it never closed green
questions.answer: Plain Red to Green; no news gap
questions.why: Plain Red to Green. The News Failure is the same trigger on a 4% news gap with a named catalyst and twice the volume.
questions.lesson_line: Same trigger, but the news and the gap make the News Failure.

wrong.News Failure; it reclaimed the close: A News Failure needs a big news gap, 4%, with a named catalyst and twice the volume.
wrong.Neither; it never closed green: Our Red to Green trigger applies to any day that reclaims the prior close.

questions.story: A stock gaps down 1% on normal volume with no headline, then reclaims the prior close.

questions.q: News Gapper or News Failure?
choices: News Gapper; the headline was good
News Failure; it closed red
Bear gap; the stock fell
questions.answer: News Failure; it closed red
questions.why: News Failure. Good news gapped it up and it closed red, under the prior close. A News Gapper holds the gap.
questions.lesson_line: Read the close against the prior close. Same headline, opposite trade.

wrong.News Gapper; the headline was good: A News Gapper closes green and holds the gap. This one closed red.
wrong.Bear gap; the stock fell: A bear gap starts with bad news. This was good news.

questions.story: A contract headline gaps a stock up 8%, and it closes 2% under the prior close.

questions.q: News Failure or earnings breakdown?
choices: News Failure; the headline was bad
News Gapper; the gap was big
Earnings breakdown; the news worked
questions.answer: Earnings breakdown; the news worked
questions.why: Earnings breakdown. Bad news gapped it down and it stayed down, so the news worked.
questions.lesson_line: If the gap keeps going, the news worked. Don't call it a failure.

wrong.News Failure; the headline was bad: A News Failure long closes back over the prior close. This one stayed down.
wrong.News Gapper; the gap was big: A News Gapper is a good-news gap that holds.

questions.story: An earnings miss gaps a stock down 9%. It closes at the low of the day, near the open.

questions.q: News Failure or Oops Reversal?
choices: Oops Reversal; there is no catalyst
News Failure; it reclaimed the close
News Gapper; it went green
questions.answer: Oops Reversal; there is no catalyst
questions.why: Oops Reversal. An Oops needs no news; a News Failure needs a dated catalyst behind the gap.
questions.lesson_line: No catalyst, no News Failure. That is an Oops.

wrong.News Failure; it reclaimed the close: A News Failure needs a dated catalyst behind the gap.
wrong.News Gapper; it went green: A News Gapper needs good news and a gap up.

questions.story: A stock opens under the prior low and reclaims the prior close. There is no news anywhere.

questions.q: What does that tell you about the news?
choices: Twelve strong signals; short them all
The news was the market, not one stock
Each one is a separate catalyst
questions.answer: The news was the market, not one stock
questions.why: The news was the market, not the stock. Fewer than 5 such events on the same day is the line.
questions.lesson_line: A cluster of the same shape means a market story.

wrong.Twelve strong signals; short them all: A cluster means the news was the market, not the stock.
wrong.Each one is a separate catalyst: A same-day cluster is one market story.

questions.story: Twelve stocks show the bearish News Failure shape on the same day.

questions.q: What does that close tell you?
choices: Nothing; one close proves nothing
The trade is working; add more
The failure itself failed
questions.answer: The failure itself failed
questions.why: The failure itself failed. The next session closed back on the news side of the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: A close back on the news side means the failure failed.

wrong.Nothing; one close proves nothing: It is an invalidation. The failure itself failed.
wrong.The trade is working; add more: No adds. A close back on the news side says the idea failed.

questions.story: You bought the red-to-green on the news day. The next session closes under the pre-news close.

questions.q: Buy at market?
choices: No; it is over 4% past the trigger
Yes; it is still climbing
Yes, but only with half size
questions.answer: No; it is over 4% past the trigger
questions.why: No. 90.50 is more than 4% above the 86.35 prior close. Chasing costs size, not risk, so we skip it.
questions.lesson_line: Past 4% over the trigger, skip it. Miss it and move on.

wrong.Yes; it is still climbing: 90.50 is more than 4% above the 86.35 trigger. We skip it.
wrong.Yes, but only with half size: Half size does not fix a chase.

questions.story: The prior close was 86.35. When you check at 2:30, the stock trades at 90.50.

questions.q: Do you buy the red-to-green?
choices: Yes; the news is different
No; a report is within 3 sessions
Yes; the stock is strong
questions.answer: No; a report is within 3 sessions
questions.why: No. No new buy in the 3 sessions before a scheduled report. The news failure was a different catalyst, but the report is near.
questions.lesson_line: A report within 3 sessions: wait.

wrong.Yes; the news is different: A report within 3 sessions blocks a new buy, whatever the other news.
wrong.Yes; the stock is strong: Strength does not move the earnings rule.

questions.story: A stock gaps down on a conference headline and comes back over the prior close. Its earnings report is 2 sessions away.

questions.q: Is it a long?
choices: Yes; the shape is strong
Yes, with a tight stop
No; a long under the 200-day
questions.answer: No; a long under the 200-day
questions.why: No. The long needs a close above the 200-day, and 282.76 is under 288.05. No longs below the 200-day, unless parabolic.
questions.lesson_line: Right shape, wrong side of the 200-day. Pass.

wrong.Yes; the shape is strong: A strong shape under the 200-day is still the wrong side of the line.
wrong.Yes, with a tight stop: No longs below the 200-day, unless parabolic.

questions.story: A stock gaps down 5.2% on 2.1x volume and closes up 5.3% in the top 7% of the range. It closes at 282.76, under its 200-day at 288.05.

questions.q: Is it a short?
choices: No; shorts go under the 200-day
Yes; a 2.7x volume fade is enough
Yes, if the stop is tight enough
questions.answer: No; shorts go under the 200-day
questions.why: No. Shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless it is a parabolic short. This close is above it.
questions.lesson_line: Shorts live below the 200-day. This one is above.

wrong.Yes; a 2.7x volume fade is enough: Shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless parabolic.
wrong.Yes, if the stop is tight enough: A tight stop does not move the 200-day rule.

questions.story: Good news gaps a stock up 5.0% on 2.7x volume. It closes down 0.2% in the bottom 18% of the range, at 377.76, above its 200-day at 358.04.

questions.q: Which gate fails the News Failure?
choices: The close; it did not finish green
The 4% gap; the open was only 3.1%
The volume; 2.5x is still too low
questions.answer: The 4% gap; the open was only 3.1%
questions.why: The 4% gap. The open was only 3.1% under the prior close, so it is a Red to Green day, not this setup.
questions.lesson_line: Check the gap size. Under 4% is a Red to Green, not a News Failure.

wrong.The close; it did not finish green: The close was strong. The open was too small a gap.
wrong.The volume; 2.5x is still too low: The test needs 2 times the volume, and 2.5x clears it.

questions.story: A stock opens 3.1% under the prior close on 2.5x volume after a 34% fall. Then it closes 4.5% up in the top 1% of the range.

questions.q: Which grades higher?
choices: The mid-range one; it held a gain
They grade the same
The full reversal near the top
questions.answer: The full reversal near the top
questions.why: The full reversal near the top. The gap is erased and the close sits near the far end of the range, an A+ cue.
questions.lesson_line: Near the high of the day is a full reversal. Mid-range is weaker.

wrong.The mid-range one; it held a gain: It reclaimed the prior close but not near the far end of the range. The A+ shape is the full reversal.
wrong.They grade the same: A full reversal near the far end of the range grades higher.

questions.story: Two bad-news gaps close back over the prior close. One closes in the top 5% of its range, 29% up. The other closes 0.8% up, in the middle of its range.

questions.q: What is missing from the picture?
choices: Crowding; it was not stretched first
Volume; 2.7x is too thin
The close; it was only 4.9% up
questions.answer: Crowding; it was not stretched first
questions.why: Crowding. With no crowding before the news, Shapiro would not trade it. MRVL stopped out the next session.
questions.lesson_line: A reversal with nothing stretched behind it is a weak read.

wrong.Volume; 2.7x is too thin: The stand-in needs 2 times the volume, and 2.7x clears it.
wrong.The close; it was only 4.9% up: The close was strong. It is the lack of a stretched market before the news.

questions.story: A stock gaps down 6.2% on 2.7x volume and closes up 4.9% in the top 12% of its range. It had fallen only 7% beforehand.

questions.q: What do you do about the stop?
choices: Tighten it to 3% and buy full size
Size from the stop, or skip
Skip the stop and watch the close
questions.answer: Size from the stop, or skip
questions.why: Size from the stop, or skip. The size comes from the stop, and if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, size second. Never tighten to fit.

wrong.Tighten it to 3% and buy full size: Never tighten the stop to make the size work.
wrong.Skip the stop and watch the close: Every position has a real stop order.

questions.story: Bad news gapped a stock down 8%. It is back over the prior close at 2:30. The news day's low is 11% under the price.

questions.q: Is the short in line with the reading?
choices: Yes; the stock faded
Yes; Green means full risk
No; it wants Orange or Red
questions.answer: No; it wants Orange or Red
questions.why: No. The short wants an Orange or Red reading, with good news being sold across the market. In a Green market the stock got carried back up.
questions.lesson_line: Shorts like Orange and Red. A Green, bought market carries the stock back.

wrong.Yes; the stock faded: The short wants an Orange or Red reading, with good news sold across the market.
wrong.Yes; Green means full risk: Green is full risk for longs. The short wants Orange or Red.

questions.story: Good news gaps a stock up 6.2% on 2.2x volume, and it sells to the low of the day. The market reading is Green and the market is being bought.

questions.q: Is a 1% up-close a failure?
choices: Yes, a quiet one: top of the range
No; a failure needs a 10% close
No; it must close beyond the prior high
questions.answer: Yes, a quiet one: top of the range
questions.why: Yes, a quiet one. A 1% up-close in the top 2% of the range on 6.5x volume is the quiet version of the reversal.
questions.lesson_line: Where it closes in the range matters as much as how far.

wrong.No; a failure needs a 10% close: The strength is in where it closes in the range, not the size of the gain.
wrong.No; it must close beyond the prior high: That is the A+ cue, not the minimum.

questions.story: Bad news gaps a stock down 4.3% on 6.5x volume. It closes only 1.0% up, but in the top 2% of its range, in a clean uptrend.

questions.q: Which news makes the better read?
choices: The vague note; it fooled nobody
The earnings miss on heavy volume
Neither; news never matters
questions.answer: The earnings miss on heavy volume
questions.why: The earnings miss on heavy volume. Small or unclear news, with volume barely above normal, is a B- cue.
questions.lesson_line: Big, clear news and heavy volume make the stronger read.

wrong.The vague note; it fooled nobody: Small or unclear news with volume barely above normal is a B- cue.
wrong.Neither; news never matters: The news matters. A big, clear catalyst is the stronger read.

questions.story: Two bad-news reversals close green. One follows a major earnings miss on heavy volume. The other follows a vague analyst note on thin volume.

questions.q: What does the 8.9% stop do to the trade?
choices: Nothing; the shape is textbook
It tightens to 3% so the size fits
Size comes down, or you skip it
questions.answer: Size comes down, or you skip it
questions.why: Size comes down, or you skip it. The stop is far wider than 3%, so size down or skip.
questions.lesson_line: A wide stop means a small size, or no trade.

wrong.Nothing; the shape is textbook: A stop far wider than 3% is a B- cue and forces a small size.
wrong.It tightens to 3% so the size fits: Never tighten the stop to make the size work.

questions.story: HIMS, 2025. An earnings gap down 8.5% on 5.2x volume closes 18.1% up. The stop is 8.9% under the buy.

questions.q: Bought at 41.89 with the stop at 38.18. The 3R price is what percent over the buy?
questions.why: 26.6. With a stop this wide, 3R is a move of more than a quarter, so the trims are rarely reached.
questions.lesson_line: A wide stop pushes 3R far away. Count the percent before you buy.

questions.q: Do you chase it?
choices: No; it is past the 4% limit
Yes; the trend is clear
Yes, but with a tight stop
questions.answer: No; it is past the 4% limit
questions.why: No. It is more than 4% past the trigger, so we skip it. Shapiro: I miss a trade, I miss it.
questions.lesson_line: Miss it and move on. The next trigger is a new trade.

wrong.Yes; the trend is clear: A clear trend does not lift the 4% limit.
wrong.Yes, but with a tight stop: A tight stop does not fix a chase.

questions.story: A news failure long closes strong, but you were away at the open. The next morning the stock is up 6% over the prior close.

questions.q: What does that tell you?
choices: A dip to buy more at the new low
The turn was not picked; stop hit
Hold until the close, then decide
questions.answer: The turn was not picked; stop hit
questions.why: The turn was not picked. Price taking out the news day's extreme is the stop.
questions.lesson_line: A new low under the news day's low is the exit.

wrong.A dip to buy more at the new low: No adds. A new low means the turn was not picked.
wrong.Hold until the close, then decide: The stop is a real order with the broker and it has been hit.

questions.story: You hold a News Failure long. Price falls through the news day's low.

questions.q: A News Failure that is a partial fade, still closing on the news side, grades B- or lower.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A partial fade, off the high but still closing on the news side, is a B- cue. MSFT 2025-07-31 closed up 3.9% after a fade.
questions.lesson_line: A fade that still closes on the news side is a weak read.

questions.q: Does the gap pass the stand-in?
choices: No; the gap is under 4%
No; it needed 5x volume
Yes; over 4% on over 2x volume
questions.answer: Yes; over 4% on over 2x volume
questions.why: Yes. A 5.5% gap down on 2.1x volume clears 4% and 2 times. AAOI reached 3R in 1 day.
questions.lesson_line: A 4% gap on 2 times the volume is the bar. AAOI cleared it.

wrong.No; the gap is under 4%: Five and a half percent is over 4%.
wrong.No; it needed 5x volume: The stand-in needs 2 times the volume or more.

questions.story: AAOI, 2026. A gap of 5.5% down on 2.1x volume, a 33% shakeout inside a leader's run. It closes 20.3% over the prior close.

questions.q: Where is the long buy?
choices: As it trades back over the prior close
At the next morning's open if it holds
At the news day's low, with a limit
questions.answer: As it trades back over the prior close
questions.why: As it trades back over the prior close, a market order. SEDG's buy was 31.83, and it reached 3R the next day.
questions.lesson_line: The buy is the trade back over the prior close.

wrong.At the next morning's open if it holds: The buy is on the news day, as price trades back over the prior close.
wrong.At the news day's low, with a limit: The low is the stop, not the buy.

questions.story: SEDG, 2025. An earnings gap down 4.1% into the 50-day, then a close 28.9% over the prior close at 0.95 of the range.

questions.q: Why is HIMS a good read but a hard trade?
choices: The shape is weak but the stop is tight
Strong shape, but a wide stop
The volume was too low
questions.answer: Strong shape, but a wide stop
questions.why: The shape is strong, but the stop is wide. At 8.9% the size comes down or the trade is skipped.
questions.lesson_line: A great reversal can still be a hard trade at the stop.

wrong.The shape is weak but the stop is tight: The reverse: the shape is strong and the stop is wide.
wrong.The volume was too low: Volume was 5.2 times, which is heavy.

questions.story: HIMS, 2025. A 43% fall, an 8.5% gap down, then a close 18.1% up. The stop is 8.9% under the buy.

questions.q: What does it show about the shape?
choices: A full A+; every cue is there
A news gapper; it closed up
The shape without the crowding
questions.answer: The shape without the crowding
questions.why: The shape without the crowding. With no crowding before the news, Shapiro would not trade it, but this leader still ran.
questions.lesson_line: The shape without the crowding is a weaker read.

wrong.A full A+; every cue is there: Without a stretched market before the news, Shapiro would not trade it.
wrong.A news gapper; it closed up: A News Gapper is a good-news gap. This gap was bad news.

questions.story: CELH, 2024. A leader above all its averages gaps down 5.7% on earnings on 7.4x volume. It falls 1% over 60 sessions and closes 20.4% up.

questions.q: Which close grades the short up?
choices: Bottom of the range, under the 200-day
The top of the range, over the 200-day
Right at the prior close, in a small bar
questions.answer: Bottom of the range, under the 200-day
questions.why: The bottom of the range, under the 200-day. The short closes in the bottom 25%, a key-reversal bar.
questions.lesson_line: The short mirrors the long: a close at the low of the day.

wrong.The top of the range, over the 200-day: The short wants a close in the bottom 25%.
wrong.Right at the prior close, in a small bar: A close at the prior close shows no reversal.

questions.story: SKIN, 2022. An earnings gap up 4.8% after a 54% run. Then a close 16.2% down at the low of the day, under the 200-day.

questions.q: Was the loss a rule break?
choices: Yes; you should have held through
No; a planned loss on a thin idea
Yes; the volume was too low to trust
questions.answer: No; a planned loss on a thin idea
questions.why: No. The rules were followed, and the stop did its job. The idea was thin: only a 7% pullback, with no crowding behind it.
questions.lesson_line: A planned loss on a thin read is the cost of the system.

wrong.Yes; you should have held through: The stop is the exit. Holding through it breaks the rule.
wrong.Yes; the volume was too low to trust: Volume was 2.7 times. The idea was thin because nothing was stretched first.

questions.story: MRVL, 2026. A 6.2% gap down on 2.7x volume closes up 4.9% in the top 12% of the range. You buy; the 8% stop is hit the next session.

questions.q: What happened to the idea?
choices: Nothing; it just needed time
It was a News Gapper all along
The failure itself failed
questions.answer: The failure itself failed
questions.why: The failure itself failed. It reached 0.9R, then reversed up through the news day's high, and the stop took it.
questions.lesson_line: A reversal can reverse again. The stop pays for it.

wrong.Nothing; it just needed time: Price took out the news day's high. That is the stop.
wrong.It was a News Gapper all along: A News Gapper holds the gap on day one. This one closed red.

questions.story: ZTS, 2025. Good news gaps it up 5.4% and it closes 3.7% down. You short. It reaches 0.9R, then reverses up through the news day's high.

questions.q: What should the stop width have told you?
choices: Skip it, or size it very small
Nothing; the crowded case is ideal
Tighten the stop to 3%
questions.answer: Skip it, or size it very small
questions.why: Skip it, or size it very small. The usual stop is within about 3%, and 11.8% needs a tiny size. It was gone in five sessions.
questions.lesson_line: A great setup with a huge stop is a skip or a tiny size.

wrong.Nothing; the crowded case is ideal: The crowded case is good, but a stop that wide breaks the usual 3%.
wrong.Tighten the stop to 3%: Never tighten the stop to make the size work.

questions.story: TTD, 2022. A 27% fall, then an earnings gap down 4.6% on 3.5x volume, a close 0.5% up in the top 8%. The stop is 11.8% under the buy.

questions.q: What did the trade miss?
choices: The volume; it was too thin to hold
The market; Green carried it back
The 200-day; it was still above it
questions.answer: The market; Green carried it back
questions.why: The market reading. A short in a Green market, with good news being bought across the market, got carried back up.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market first. A Green market carries a failed short back.

wrong.The volume; it was too thin to hold: Volume was 2.2 times. The market is what carried it back.
wrong.The 200-day; it was still above it: The reading was the problem here: Green and bought.

questions.story: UAL, 2020. Good news gaps it up 6.2% and it sells to near the low. You short in a Green market. Two sessions later it is back through the day's high.

questions.q: What did the cluster hint at?
choices: Two strong, separate shorts
A stock-specific catalyst each
Market-wide news, then a rally
questions.answer: Market-wide news, then a rally
questions.why: Market-wide news. Both shorts were stopped on 2025-04-09, the day the market rallied. A same-day cluster means the news was the market.
questions.lesson_line: When many names fade at once, it is the market, not the stock.

wrong.Two strong, separate shorts: Many names showing one shape on one day means the news was the market.
wrong.A stock-specific catalyst each: The same shape on the same day points to the market.

questions.story: On 2025-04-08, 56 stocks show the good-news failure shape. Two of them, AMAT and DAL, gap up 4.2% on 2.2x volume and close in the bottom 11% of the range. Both stops are hit the next day.

questions.q: How do you answer?
choices: No; alone it showed no edge
He is right; most win
Yes; the trims make it a sure win
questions.answer: No; alone it showed no edge
questions.why: No. In our test it showed no stand-alone edge: about two losses for every 3R winner. Never size up on a win-rate claim.
questions.lesson_line: Alone, it showed no edge in our test. Never size up on a win-rate claim.

wrong.He is right; most win: In the test only 33.4% reached 3R before the stop. That is not a high hit rate.
wrong.Yes; the trims make it a sure win: Nothing is sure. The test used a fixed stop with no trims, so it does not say how our plan would do.

questions.story: A friend says a News Failure wins most of the time, so size up. Our test of 1,534 events found 33.4% reached 3R and 17.9% reached 5R before the stop.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, a news day after the close. It gapped down on heavy volume. Was there a valid red-to-green long that day?
choices: Not valid; the close stayed under it
Valid; it traded back over the close
Not valid; it gapped down, so it is weak
questions.answer: Valid; it traded back over the close
questions.why: Valid. A 5.5% gap down on 2.1x volume traded back over the prior close. It finished 20.3% over it, a 33% shakeout inside a leader's run. It reached 3R in 1 day.

It hurts; breadth should be strong
questions.answer: A washed-out market agrees with the long

questions.q: The stop for a News Failure short goes a few cents under the news day's low.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. A few cents beyond the news day's extreme so far: under the low for a long, over the high for a short.
questions.lesson_line: Long: under the low. Short: over the high.

questions.q: A News Failure long is bought at the open on the news day.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The buy is a market order as price trades back over the prior close on the news day, not at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Wait for the trade back over the prior close.

questions.q: A close in the top quarter after a gap down guarantees a News Failure will work.
questions.answer: False
